answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to maintain a continuous proof-of-work pulse: small, periodic computations tied to a unique identity key, like a juniper tree whose roots anchor it in one place. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real compute and time, and each fake pulse adds latency an observer can detect. When one identity is caught cheating, the penalty ripples through its linked reputation graph, so a single bad actor loses every identity it controls at once.
